films.description:
Cornell Cinema is delighted to welcome new Cornell students for a special Orientation Week screening of Thelma & Louise (1991)!


Before the film, you can enjoy a sneak preview of films and series on offer this fall, participate in a friendly movie trivia competition, and learn more about how you can get involved with the cinema during your time at Cornell. Free popcorn will be provided, and we’ll be raffling off prizes like movie tickets, All-Access Passes, and Cornell Cinema swag. We can’t wait to see you there!


About the film

Thelma, a bored housewife, and Louise, a strait-laced waitress at a coffee shop, are best friends who are sick of the life they have settled for. 

Eager to escape the tedium of their everyday lives, the pair sneak off in Louise’s ’66 Thunderbird convertible for a three-day fishing trip with no husbands, no boyfriends, and no problems. But things don’t go quite according to plan when an encounter with a drunken, foul-mouthed, would-be rapist transforms their quiet getaway into a cross-country escape that will change their lives forever.


A quintessential feminist road movie that polarized audiences when it was first released, Thelma and Louise have secured their place as one of the toughest and most memorable dynamic duos in cinematic history.


Free admission! This event is offered in partnership with the Tatkon Center for New Students and open only to new Cornell students as part of New Student Orientation 2026.


Thelma & Louise has been digitally restored from a new 4K 16 bit scan, supervised by director Ridley Scott using the original negative, in honor of its 35th anniversary. The film has been restored by The Criterion Collection with participation from MGM Studios and Park Circus. 


Part of our "Restorations & Rediscoveries" series. Courtesy: Park Circus Films

In this animated psychological thriller from Japanese auteur Satoshi Kon, Mima Kirigoe, a former pop idol, makes a bold transition into acting, taking on a controversial acting role. Her dramatic reinvention grabs public attention, but also provokes unease among her fans, her manager, and even herself as she struggles with the rapid shift from her days as a pop idol. 


After a stalker begins to shadow her, and a screenwriter and a photographer are murdered one after another, Mima slowing begins to lost her grip on reality and wonders if a split personality is gradually taking over, just like the character that she plays in the drama. Her sense of insanity deepens when “the other Mima” the pop idol who was supposed to have “graduated,” appears in front of her...


Hailed as the first animated film to feature an authentic psychological suspense story and newly restored in 4K, Perfect Blue unfolds like an optical illusion that blends fiction and reality, dreams and delusions, and cyberspace and continues to unnerve audiences nearly twenty years after its initial release.

Cady becomes instant friends with outsiders Damian and Janis — that is, until she meets the Plastics, the three most popular, beautiful girls of North Shore High School. Cady is hesitant when the Plastics immediately let Cady into their group, but Damien and Janis convince her to develop her friendship with the Plastics so they can learn their deepest, darkest secrets. films.name: The Producers
films.description:
Filmed over thirty years before Nathan Lane and Matthew Broderick starred in the smash hit remake based on the Broadway show, The Producers remains "one of the funniest movies ever made." (Roger Ebert) 


The unforgettable Zero Mostel stars as Max Bialystock, a conniving, washed-up Broadway producer, who determines in consultation with his mild-mannered accountant Leo Bloom (Gene Wilder, in one of his first comedic roles) that he can make more money with a flop than a hit. Their plan? To convince charming wealthy old biddies to invest in an overbudget production, then put on a sure-fire disaster, so nobody will ask for their money back — and what's more disastrous than a tasteless musical celebrating Adolf Hitler.


With a chorus line of jackbooted frauleins and lyrics like "Don’t be stupid, be a smarty! Come and join the Nazi Party!," Bialystock settles back to wait for the fall and collect his cash, but "Springtime for Hitler" is an unexpected hit!


With unforgettable performances by Mostel and Wilder, The Producers is frenzied, audacious, achingly funny, and Mel Brooks at his very best.


Part of our "Happy Birthday, Mel Brooks!" series. Courtesy: Rialto Pictures

films.name: Cutting Through Rocks
films.short_description: 37-year-old Sara Shahverdi, a motorcycle riding, land owning, former midwife-turned-fierce citizen advocate and recent divorcée, just won a landslide local election in her remote Iranian village and everyone has an opinion about it.
films.description:
Winner of the World Cinema Documentary Grand Jury Prize at the 2025 Sundance Film Festival, Cutting Through Rocks is an inspiring story of determination and civic courage.


37-year-old Sara Shahverdi, a motorcycle riding, land owning, former midwife-turned-fierce citizen advocate and recent divorcée, just won a landslide local election to become the first elected councilwoman in her remote village in northwest Iran. Shahverdi aims to use her position to break long-held patriarchal traditions by training teenage girls to ride motorcycles and stopping child marriages. When accusations arise questioning Sara’s intentions to empower local girls, her identity is put in turmoil, making her bold dreams feel impossible to realize.


Filmed over several years, Cutting Through Rocks is an intimate portrait of Shahverdi's determined efforts to upend daily injustices and improve the lives of women in her town.


In Azerbaijani, Turkish, Arabic, and Persian with English subtitles. Part of our "Doc Spots" series. Courtesy: Autlook Filmsales

films.name: Aguirre, the Wrath of God
films.short_description: A few decades after the destruction of the Inca Empire, a Spanish expedition led by the infamous Aguirre leaves the mountains of Peru and goes down the Amazon River in search of the lost city of El Dorado. When great difficulties arise, Aguirre’s men start to wonder whether their quest will lead them to prosperity or certain death.
films.description:
In 1560, a few decades after the destruction of the Inca Empire, an expedition led by the infamous Aguirre (Klaus Kinski) leaves the mountains of Peru and goes down the Amazon River in search of the lost city of El Dorado. When great difficulties arise, Aguirre’s men start to wonder whether their quest will lead them to prosperity or certain death.


Werner Herzog’s haunting film brings to the screen one of the bloodiest and most bizarre footnotes in the history of the Spanish conquests in the Americas. Although the exact outcome of this disappeared expedition is unclear, Herzog weaves a possible tale of murder and insanity propelled by Aguirre’s lust to found his own dynasty in South America.


Aided by its striking cinematography, an immersive soundscape captured on location during an arduous five-week shoot in the Peruvian rainforest, and a haunting choral score, Aguirre, the Wrath of God is a hallucinatory period drama, a hermetic world of madness and decay that also serves as commentary on fascism in the 20th century.


In German, Quechua, and Spanish with English subtitles. Part of our "Wayfaring Stranger" series. Courtesy: Shout! Factory/Swank Motion Pictures

films.name: Xiao Wu / Pickpocket
films.short_description: A small town pickpocket whose friends have moved on to higher trades finds himself bitter and unable to adapt.
films.description:
One of cinema’s great debuts, this film by the generation-defining Chinese auteur Jia Zhangke is a searing first expression of his signature theme: the disillusionment of people left behind by a society modernizing at whiplash speed. 


Shot on 16 mm with nonprofessional actors and without state approval, Xiao Wu (also known in English as Pickpocket ) enfolds its critique within a subtly ironic study of a cocky, aimless pickpocket (Wang Hongwei) who, as those around him advance thanks to the opportunities of the new market economy, finds himself increasingly alienated. A budding relationship with a brothel worker (Hao Hongjian) seems to offer him a sense of meaning—but is it as illusory as the promises of capitalism? 


Already a master of the slow-burn long takes, minimalist framing, and meaningful silences that would become his trademarks, Jia fashions a quietly shattering portrait of humanity caught in the jaws of globalization.


In Mandarin with English subtitles. Part of our "Wayfaring Strangers" series. Courtesy: Janus Films

films.name: Fast Times at Ridgemont High
films.description:
In Amy Heckerling’s (Clueless) brashly funny yet sensitive comedy, a group of Southern-California high school students ignore their studies in favor of indulging in their teenage distractions: sex, drugs, and rock 'n' roll.


The film follows the fortunes of Ridgemont High senior Brad Hamilton (Reinhold) and his freshman sister Stacy (Jason Leigh) during a year when hormones are flaring. In this animated psychological thriller from Japanese auteur Satoshi Kon, Mima Kirigoe, a former pop idol, makes a bold transition into acting, taking on a controversial acting role. films.name: Vagabond
films.description:
Mona Bergeron is dead, her frozen body found in a ditch in the French countryside. From this, the film flashes back to the weeks leading up to her death. Through these flashbacks, Mona gradually declines as she travels from place to place, taking odd jobs and staying with whomever will offer her a place to sleep. Mona is fiercely independent, craving freedom over comfort, but it is this desire to be free that will eventually lead to her demise.


Sandrine Bonnaire won the Best Actress César for her portrayal of the defiant young drifter Mona. Agnès Varda pieces together Mona’s story through flashbacks told by those who encountered her (played by a largely nonprofessional cast), producing a splintered portrait of an enigmatic woman. With its sparse, poetic imagery, Vagabond (French title: Sans toit ni loi) is a stunner, and won Varda the top prize at the Venice Film Festival in 1985.

Werner Herzog’s haunting film brings to the screen one of the bloodiest and most bizarre footnotes in the history of the Spanish conquests in the Americas. Aided by its striking cinematography, an immersive soundscape captured on location during an arduous five-week shoot in the Peruvian rainforest, and a haunting choral score, Aguirre, the Wrath of God is a hallucinatory period drama, a hermetic world of madness and decay that also serves as commentary on fascism in the 20th century.

films.description:
Filmmaker Ross McElwee has spent forty years recording himself and his family, creating documentaries that chronicle the shifting contours of American society through the lens of personal history. His son Adrian grew up inside those films, and eventually began experimenting with the camera himself. When a Hollywood producer acquires the rights to adapt McElwee’s 1986 breakthrough Sherman's March into a work of fiction, twenty-year-old Adrian sees a chance for his father to finally reach a wider audience. As the adaptation stalls, Adrian gets swept into a deepening drug addiction and dies from a fentanyl overdose, leaving behind hours of personal video footage.


Retracing Adrian’s final years, McElwee reckons with what his camera captured and what remained hauntingly out of frame. As he reflects on a lifetime behind the camera, Ross’s own effort to remix and remake the movie that Adrian never got to finish takes on new significance. An ever-expanding hall of mirrors built from decades of home movies, REMAKE is both McElwee’s attempt to hold onto his son, and to let him go.

films.description:
One of cinema’s great debuts, this film by the generation-defining Chinese auteur Jia Zhangke is a searing first expression of his signature theme: the disillusionment of people left behind by a society modernizing at whiplash speed. 


Shot on 16 mm with nonprofessional actors and without state approval, Xiao Wu (also known in English as Pickpocket ) enfolds its critique within a subtly ironic study of a cocky, aimless pickpocket (Wang Hongwei) who, as those around him advance thanks to the opportunities of the new market economy, finds himself increasingly alienated. A budding relationship with a brothel worker (Hao Hongjian) seems to offer him a sense of meaning—but is it as illusory as the promises of capitalism? 


Already a master of the slow-burn long takes, minimalist framing, and meaningful silences that would become his trademarks, Jia fashions a quietly shattering portrait of humanity caught in the jaws of globalization.

films.name: Bombshell
films.description:
Eighty years after the devastating atomic bombings that ushered in the nuclear age, Bombshell explores how the U.S. government manipulated the narrative about the atomic bombings of the Japanese cities Hiroshima and Nagasaki. Through propaganda, censorship and the co-opting of the press, the government presented a benevolent picture of atomic power, minimizing the horrific human toll. Bombshell sheds light on the efforts of a group of intrepid reporters to let the world know the truth.


On August 6, 1945, a revolutionary new weapon destroyed Hiroshima, a Japanese city of 300,000 inhabitants. Three days later, a second atomic bomb was dropped on Nagasaki. America’s secret superweapon was lauded for bringing about victory in the Pacific and ending World War II. President Truman’s official announcement includes half-truths that shape the government’s official narrative: “Sixteen hours ago, an American airplane dropped one bomb on Hiroshima, an important Japanese army base.” In fact, the bomb was aimed at Hiroshima’s city center for maximum psychological effect; the army base on its outskirts escaped much damage.


The U.S. media became pivotal in promoting — and then piercing — the official narrative. While Truman publicly declared that “it has never been the habit of the scientists of this country or this government to withhold from the world scientific knowledge,” that is precisely what General Groves, leader of the Manhattan Project, insisted upon. His strategy was a PR campaign fueled by press releases written anonymously by William L. Laurence, the science writer for The New York Times and an undercover member of the Manhattan Project team. Laurence’s assignment: downplay the radiation effects from the bomb.


There will be a post-screening discussion after the film, moderated by Rebecca Slayton, Director of the Judith Reppy Institute for Peace and Conflict Studies.


Free admission! Sponsored by the Reppy Institute for Peace and Conflict Studies.

films.description:
Overburden is a feature documentary set in the mist-shrouded Nimba Mountains on the Liberia–Guinea border, where rare wildlife and local communities reclaim a landscape scarred by mining. Today, this fragile recovery faces a new threat: a global steel company using conservation promises to brand a new mining venture as green.


Founded in the wake of war, the East Nimba Nature Reserve shelters some of West Africa’s most endangered species. With exclusive, on-the-ground access, Overburden follows rangers, scientists, and forest defenders, including ranger Moses Darpey, biologist Grace Kotee Zansi, chief park warden Catherine Kuku Dolo, and community leaders Saye Thompson and Dada Konkah, who tend the land, protecting endangered species and sustaining livelihoods as a billion-dollar company falls short of promised support. They are joined by Shadrach Kerwillain, a Liberian conservation biologist and Mnqobi Mamba, a bat scientist from Eswatini, who navigate the tangled frontier where mining meets conservation and where memory, science, and power collide.


The film captures their intimate encounters with the mountain’s extraordinary inhabitants, from the only true viviparous toad found nowhere else on Earth to resilient cave-dwelling bats and adaptive chimpanzees. Grace works to reconcile clashing farmers and chimpanzees through coexistence strategies. Moses searches for the rare Nimba toad on high peaks, while Mnqobi revisits a cave to see if the bats he helped relocate as part of the company’s biodiversity offset program are still there.


Overburden tells a powerful story of resilience and transformation in a landscape shaped by an invasive industry yet alive with possibility. Through vivid cinematography and deeply rooted storytelling, the film follows communities and nature enduring and adapting in the face of relentless global forces. Overburden celebrates the power of mutual aid, showing how people and ecosystems persist, rebuild, and thrive against overwhelming odds.


Creative producer Gregg Mitman will join for a conversation after the film with Cornell faculty members, moderated by Rachel Bezner Kerr, Director of the Institute for African Development.

Amid stifling heat and pervasive drought, Isabel (Jorrybell Agoto), a 17-year-old Ilokana from the rural north, works at a posh country club outside Manila, lining up golf balls for powerful men to drive into the verdant horizon. New to the job, she wanders the immaculate grounds sampling its luxuries as members, including an industrialist and his expatriate niece, the club president and his pampered wife, and a slew of Chinese tourists, engage in a complex dance with the club’s doting and subservient staff.


But something is rotting beneath the pristine fairways of the elite resort, as Isabel discovers when she tries to return a mislaid golf club to its patriarchal director, Dr. Palanca (Teroy Guzman). The deeper she journeys into its most exclusive corners, the closer she gets to the violent truths of the club, her native Philippines, and her own past.

films.sort_key: 2026 Sundance Film Festival Short Film Tour
films.description:
The 2026 Sundance Film Festival Short Film Tour, presented by Ketel One Vodka, is a curated collection of six standout short films from this year’s Festival, including three Festival Award–winning titles. This 99-minute program offers a mix of stories that highlight bold perspectives and next-gen storytellers. 


The 2026 Sundance Film Festival Short Film Tour provides a curated glimpse into the Festival’s selections, highlighting the depth of narrative possibilities explored in the short film format. For those who couldn’t attend the 2026 Sundance Film Festival — held in person in Park City and Salt Lake City, Utah, from January 22 to February 1, as well as online — this tour invites audiences across the world to experience a collection of resonant, provocative, tender, and human-centered fiction, nonfiction, and animated shorts that showcase truly dynamic independent storytelling. 


Long recognized as a vital platform for short-form cinema, the Sundance Film Festival annually spotlights some of the boldest emerging voices in filmmaking today and has long been established as a place to discover talented directors, such as alumni Andrea Arnold, Lake Bell, Damien Chazelle, Destin Daniel Cretton, Jay and Mark Duplass, Debra Granik, Rashaad Ernesto Green, Reinaldo Marcus Green, Sterlin Harjo, Todd Haynes, Don Hertzfeldt, Sky Hopinka, Shaka King, Lynne Ramsay, Dee Rees, Joey Soloway, Taika Waititi, and many others. 


The 2026 program features:


The Boys and the Bees / U.S.A. (Director and Producer: Arielle Knight, Producer: Sean Weiner)

On an idyllic farm in rural Georgia, Black beekeeping parents tenderly share their knowledge of life, love, and nature with their young sons while restoring their homestead. 

Short Film Jury Award: Nonfiction 


Arielle Knight is an Emmy Award–winning producer and New York–based filmmaker whose work spans short and feature-length films centered on Black life and community. Supported by Sundance Institute, Ford Foundation, Catapult Film Fund, and others, she is developing hybrid projects that blur genre and reimagine form.


Crisis Actor / U.S.A. (Director, Screenwriter, and Producer: Lily Platt, Producers: Sophie Seyd, Alex Bendo, Lexi Preiser)

Fired from her day job, an impulsive actress crashes a support group and spirals into a chaotic night that forces her to face her addiction to drama. Cast: Sarah Steele, Philip Ettinger. Short Film Jury Award: U.S. Fiction


Lily Platt is a filmmaker from New York City. Platt worked as a staff producer at Story Syndicate, where she made docu-series for HBO and Netflix. She is currently pursuing a master’s degree in film at New York University’s Tisch School of the Arts. Crisis Actor is her debut short. 


Living with a Visionary / U.S.A. (Director, Screenwriter, and Producer: Stephen P. Neary, Producer: Mireia Vilanova)

After 50 years of marriage, John must care for his wife while learning to live alongside

her vivid hallucinations. Cast: James Cromwell, Katherine LaVictoire. 

Short Film Jury Award: Animation 


Stephen P. Neary is a Los Angeles–based writer, director, and storyboard artist known for creating The Fungies! for Cartoon Network/HBO Max. His credits include KPop Demon Hunters, Clarence, two Ice Age films, and Rio. He teaches at CalArts and works as a story artist for Netflix, Illumination, Annapurna, and Sony. 


Marga en el DF / Mexico, U.S.A. (Director and Screenwriter: Gabriela Ortega, Producers: Karla Luna Cantú, Natalia Gonzalez, Eugenio Valero, Carlos López Estrada, Valerie Bush, Stacy Perskie)

In the wake of Selena Quintanilla’s murder, Marga’s life takes an unexpected turn at 21 weeks pregnant during a surprise visit to Mexico City. Cast: Camila Santana, David Palacio, Xabiani Ponce de León, Andrea de Fátima. 


Gabriela Ortega is an award-winning filmmaker from the Dominican Republic. Her short film Huella premiered at the 2022 Sundance Film Festival, and its feature script participated in the Sundance Institute labs. She is developing a film for a major studio and is preparing her debut feature set in the Dominican Republic. 


Pankaja / U.S.A., India (Director, Screenwriter, and Producer: Anooya Swamy, Producers: Nakirekanti Swamy, Archana Swamy, Vindhya Gupta)

Pankaja, along with her daughter, Lalli, searches for her missing husband through the city slums of Bangalore to bring him back home. Cast: Harshini Boyalla, Padmashree G. 


Anooya Swamy is a New York–based Indian filmmaker born and raised in Bangalore, pursuing her MFA in film/TV production at Tisch School of the Arts, where she served as Spike Lee’s assistant. She is an Ang Lee Scholar, a BAFTA Scholar, and a Sundance Ignite x Adobe fellow. 


Sauna Sickness / Sweden (Director, Screenwriter, and Producer: Malin Barr)

Struggling to maintain the peace she mistakes for love, Cleo’s steamy New Year’s Eve plans fissure into a chilling nightmare. Cast: Thea Sofie Loch Næss, Adam Lundgren, Magnus Krepper, Sanna Krepper. 


Malin Barr is a Swedish writer, director, and actor working between Stockholm and Los Angeles, whose work centers on female-driven stories, blending dark humor with genre elements. She is an alum of the Alma Löv Screenwriting Academy and the Cine Qua Non Writers Lab. Her latest short film, Sauna Sickness, premiered in competition at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival and was an official selection at the Göteborg Film Festival and SXSW London, among others. films.description:
Filmmaker Ross McElwee has spent forty years recording himself and his family, creating documentaries that chronicle the shifting contours of American society through the lens of personal history. His son Adrian grew up inside those films, and eventually began experimenting with the camera himself. When a Hollywood producer acquires the rights to adapt McElwee’s 1986 breakthrough Sherman's March into a work of fiction, twenty-year-old Adrian sees a chance for his father to finally reach a wider audience. As the adaptation stalls, Adrian gets swept into a deepening drug addiction and dies from a fentanyl overdose, leaving behind hours of personal video footage.


Retracing Adrian’s final years, McElwee reckons with what his camera captured and what remained hauntingly out of frame. As he reflects on a lifetime behind the camera, Ross’s own effort to remix and remake the movie that Adrian never got to finish takes on new significance. An ever-expanding hall of mirrors built from decades of home movies, REMAKE is both McElwee’s attempt to hold onto his son, and to let him go.

Mona Bergeron is dead, her frozen body found in a ditch in the French countryside. From this, the film flashes back to the weeks leading up to her death. films.name: The Message
films.description:
Drawing inspiration from the grandeur of Omar Sharif's performance in David Lean's Lawrence of Arabia, Syrian filmmaker Moustapha Akkad's spectacular historical epic offers a compelling account of early Islamic history. In sixth-century Mecca, Prophet Muhammad receives his first revelation from God as a messenger, who compels him to lead the people of Mecca against the corrupt political and military leaders and instead worship the one true God. Three years later, he's not alone in his quest and publicly declares his prophecy, bringing persecution and violence upon his followers.


Though the film highlights the Prophet Muhammad's teachings alongside crucial events like the Battle of Badr and Battle of Uhud, Akkad was careful not to portray the Prophet Muhammed visually or audibly, which is forbidden under Islamic law. Instead, the story is largely told from the point of view of Muhammad’s uncle Hamza and the ruler of Mecca Abu Sufian and his wife Hind with the Prophet's presence suggested off-screen by ingenious camera work.

films.name: Better Luck Tomorrow
films.description:
Better Luck Tomorrow is a pulse-pounding crime drama and the debut feature film of Taiwanese-American director Justin Lin, most notably of the Fast & Furious franchise. The film centers on a group of over-achieving Asian-American high school seniors who enjoy a newfound sense of power and brotherhood when they embrace criminal activities as their main extra-curriculars.


Accomplished high school student Ben (Parry Shen) seems to excel at almost everything except winning over his dream girl Stephanie (Karin Anna Cheung). When he begins an unlikely friendship with trouble-seeking tough guy Daric (Roger Fan), Ben and his friend Virgil (Jason Tobin) become involved in petty crime that gets increasingly dangerous, with his various illegal ventures extending to include Stephanie and her wealthy college beau Steve (John Cho). As the stakes get higher and the wild parties and drugs take their toll, Ben grows more desperate to get out and leave behind a life of crime for good. But before he can, a final devastating turn leads to a shocking finale that will stay with you long after you leave the theatre.


Among the first mainstream Hollywood films by an Asian-American director, the film was initially criticized for its violent representation of Asian-American teens, but has come to be celebrated for the intensity of its story and complexity of its characters, who have the right to be flawed, multidimensional human beings. Defying all stereotypes, Better Luck Tomorrow ultimately offers a disturbing look at the dark side of four wealthy, disaffected Southern California suburbanites.


Director Justin Lin also considers the film to be a prequel to the Fast & Furious franchise because Virgil's carefree older cousin Han is also the character Han Seoul-Oh, who is introduced in the 2006 film The Fast and the Furious: Tokyo Drift.


Part of our "Too Cool for School" series. Courtesy: Paramount Pictures/Swank Motion Pictures

films.sort_key: 2026 Sundance Film Festival Short Film Tour
films.description:
The 2026 Sundance Film Festival Short Film Tour, presented by Ketel One Vodka, is a curated collection of six standout short films from this year’s Festival, including three Festival Award–winning titles. This 99-minute program offers a mix of stories that highlight bold perspectives and next-gen storytellers. 


The 2026 Sundance Film Festival Short Film Tour provides a curated glimpse into the Festival’s selections, highlighting the depth of narrative possibilities explored in the short film format. For those who couldn’t attend the 2026 Sundance Film Festival — held in person in Park City and Salt Lake City, Utah, from January 22 to February 1, as well as online — this tour invites audiences across the world to experience a collection of resonant, provocative, tender, and human-centered fiction, nonfiction, and animated shorts that showcase truly dynamic independent storytelling. 


Long recognized as a vital platform for short-form cinema, the Sundance Film Festival annually spotlights some of the boldest emerging voices in filmmaking today and has long been established as a place to discover talented directors, such as alumni Andrea Arnold, Lake Bell, Damien Chazelle, Destin Daniel Cretton, Jay and Mark Duplass, Debra Granik, Rashaad Ernesto Green, Reinaldo Marcus Green, Sterlin Harjo, Todd Haynes, Don Hertzfeldt, Sky Hopinka, Shaka King, Lynne Ramsay, Dee Rees, Joey Soloway, Taika Waititi, and many others. 


The 2026 program features:


The Boys and the Bees / U.S.A. (Director and Producer: Arielle Knight, Producer: Sean Weiner)

On an idyllic farm in rural Georgia, Black beekeeping parents tenderly share their knowledge of life, love, and nature with their young sons while restoring their homestead. 

Short Film Jury Award: Nonfiction 


Arielle Knight is an Emmy Award–winning producer and New York–based filmmaker whose work spans short and feature-length films centered on Black life and community. Supported by Sundance Institute, Ford Foundation, Catapult Film Fund, and others, she is developing hybrid projects that blur genre and reimagine form.


Crisis Actor / U.S.A. (Director, Screenwriter, and Producer: Lily Platt, Producers: Sophie Seyd, Alex Bendo, Lexi Preiser)

Fired from her day job, an impulsive actress crashes a support group and spirals into a chaotic night that forces her to face her addiction to drama. Cast: Sarah Steele, Philip Ettinger. Short Film Jury Award: U.S. Fiction


Lily Platt is a filmmaker from New York City. Platt worked as a staff producer at Story Syndicate, where she made docu-series for HBO and Netflix. She is currently pursuing a master’s degree in film at New York University’s Tisch School of the Arts. Crisis Actor is her debut short. 


Living with a Visionary / U.S.A. (Director, Screenwriter, and Producer: Stephen P. Neary, Producer: Mireia Vilanova)

After 50 years of marriage, John must care for his wife while learning to live alongside

her vivid hallucinations. Cast: James Cromwell, Katherine LaVictoire. 

Short Film Jury Award: Animation 


Stephen P. Neary is a Los Angeles–based writer, director, and storyboard artist known for creating The Fungies! for Cartoon Network/HBO Max. His credits include KPop Demon Hunters, Clarence, two Ice Age films, and Rio. He teaches at CalArts and works as a story artist for Netflix, Illumination, Annapurna, and Sony. 


Marga en el DF / Mexico, U.S.A. (Director and Screenwriter: Gabriela Ortega, Producers: Karla Luna Cantú, Natalia Gonzalez, Eugenio Valero, Carlos López Estrada, Valerie Bush, Stacy Perskie)

In the wake of Selena Quintanilla’s murder, Marga’s life takes an unexpected turn at 21 weeks pregnant during a surprise visit to Mexico City. Cast: Camila Santana, David Palacio, Xabiani Ponce de León, Andrea de Fátima. 


Gabriela Ortega is an award-winning filmmaker from the Dominican Republic. Her short film Huella premiered at the 2022 Sundance Film Festival, and its feature script participated in the Sundance Institute labs. She is developing a film for a major studio and is preparing her debut feature set in the Dominican Republic. 


Pankaja / U.S.A., India (Director, Screenwriter, and Producer: Anooya Swamy, Producers: Nakirekanti Swamy, Archana Swamy, Vindhya Gupta)

Pankaja, along with her daughter, Lalli, searches for her missing husband through the city slums of Bangalore to bring him back home. Cast: Harshini Boyalla, Padmashree G. 


Anooya Swamy is a New York–based Indian filmmaker born and raised in Bangalore, pursuing her MFA in film/TV production at Tisch School of the Arts, where she served as Spike Lee’s assistant. She is an Ang Lee Scholar, a BAFTA Scholar, and a Sundance Ignite x Adobe fellow. 


Sauna Sickness / Sweden (Director, Screenwriter, and Producer: Malin Barr)

Struggling to maintain the peace she mistakes for love, Cleo’s steamy New Year’s Eve plans fissure into a chilling nightmare. Cast: Thea Sofie Loch Næss, Adam Lundgren, Magnus Krepper, Sanna Krepper. 


Malin Barr is a Swedish writer, director, and actor working between Stockholm and Los Angeles, whose work centers on female-driven stories, blending dark humor with genre elements. She is an alum of the Alma Löv Screenwriting Academy and the Cine Qua Non Writers Lab. Her latest short film, Sauna Sickness, premiered in competition at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival and was an official selection at the Göteborg Film Festival and SXSW London, among others. The film is represented by Premium Films (Paris) and has secured distribution with Canal+.

The deeper she journeys into its most exclusive corners, the closer she gets to the violent truths of the club, her native Philippines, and her own past.

films.name: Barbara Forever
films.short_description: An archive-driven exploration of the life, work, and legacy of iconic, pioneering lesbian filmmaker Barbara Hammer.
films.description:
"If we're experimenting with our lives and the way we're going to live, our film and our art should also be experimental. It breaks tradition, and makes you think in a broader way. It's the way I experience the world." – Barbara Hammer


BARBARA FOREVER explores the films, archive, and ongoing cultural impact of experimental filmmaker Barbara Hammer, revealing her ingenious lifelong artistic effort to create and record lesbian histories, personal and societal. Through her own images and words, the film centers Hammer as a prism of the cultural ecosystems around her – through the feminist and queer movements in 1970s San Francisco, the male-dominated New York art world of the 1980s, the New Queer Cinema movement of the 1990s, and expanded LGBTQIA+ representation in art and culture in the 2000s.


Driven by her canon of over eighty films, a vast collection of unreleased archival materials – hundreds of hours of footage, personal photographs and ephemera, and extensive audio interviews – BARBARA FOREVER tells Barbara Hammer’s story through her own voice and visual perspective, making her the expert on her life, vision, and motivations.


Barbara Hammer’s films break taboos around female sexuality, aging, illness, and queer love, often using her own body as a site of exploration and political power. Through the course of the film, she shows us that the personal is not only political, the personal is historical. Looking to Barbara Hammer as one of the first filmmakers to put a full lesbian life on screen that wasn’t there before, her work becomes a blueprint for a new generation of queer and radical artists to write their own histories into existence. This exploration of both Barbara Hammer’s life, work, archive, and her ongoing legacy provides an urgent, necessary story of queer life, feminist history, and American cinema

films.name: Cinema Pe Cinema: The Theatres. The Movies. And Us
films.sort_key: Cinema Pe Cinema: The Theatres. The Movies. And Us
films.description:
For some, India’s single-screen cinemas are a legacy to be celebrated and preserved. For others, they remain a place still frequented to see the movies. Yet others lament their widespread demise, remembering how within the dark cavernous neighborhood cinema hall or grand picture palace they first discovered the magic of the movies. However, cinema theatres are much more than just sites of nostalgia and personal memory.


The documentary Cinema Pe Cinema: The Theatres. The Movies. And Us (2024) explores the past, present, and futures of single-screen cinemas across India. While migrating films, designs, and technologies shaped these theatres, so have migrations of their people from cinema artists to owners and audiences. Symbols of family, community, and national pride, cinemas are also flashpoints for longstanding controversies over politics, sexuality, and rights to the city. As its subjects reminisce about their cinema-going experiences and connections to their lives, the film becomes an act of resistance against forgetting. But it also gives us glimpses of new lives for some iconic theatres of the past. As more and more single screens shutter across India and the world in the age of streaming and multiplexes, Cinema Pe Cinema testifies to movie theatres’ importance for fostering community during polarized times.

 

Film director and screen writer Vani Subramanian, New Delhi,  and producer and researcher Mary N. Woods, Professor Emerita, Department of Architecture, Cornell University, will join for a post-screening conversation.

 

Free admission! Sponsored by the South Asia Program and the Migrations Program at the Mario Einaudi Center for International Studies.

 

In Hindi, English, and Tamil with English subtitles. Courtesy of the filmmaker. More information at: vanishes.in

 

About the filmmakers

One-time advertising writer, Vani Subramanian has been a feminist activist and documentary filmmaker since the nineties. Her work as a filmmaker explores the connections between our everyday practices, perceptions and prejudices, and the larger political questions confronting us through the lens of everyday practices, perceptions and prejudices – be it about gender and space, sex selective abortions, sectarian intolerance, education, food practices, cinema spectatorship and culture, neighborhood histories and memory, or justice and the death penalty.

 

Vani's films have been screened and received awards, both nationally and internationally. Over the years, she has extended her practice to video art in performance, mixed media installations and pop-up digital art shows. Vani has been a Fulbright Fellow in Performing and Media Arts, Cornell University, and has also served as visiting/guest faculty at many universities in India. She is also the Creative Director of reFrame Institute of Art and Expression, an initiative that produces, mentors and disseminates artistic efforts that respond to contemporary challenges.

 

Mary N. Woods, historian of cities, architecture, and media, is the first woman to be tenured in Cornell’s Department of Architecture. She is the author of such seminal works as: Women Architects in India: Histories of Practice in Mumbai and Delhi (2016); Beyond the Architect’s Eye: Photographs of the American Built Environment (2009); and From Craft to Profession: Practice of Architecture in 19th-Century America (1999). Mary continues to publish on gender and architectural design and practice and single-screen cinemas and community in the US and India. She is now collaborating with photographer Chirodeep Chaudhuri for a work about Mumbai’s architecture of the night and with Annie Schentag, historian and preservationist, and Nipun Prabhakar, architect and photographer, for a study of the post-industrial cities of Buffalo and Bhopal and New York and Mumbai.

films.name: Better Luck Tomorrow
films.description:
Better Luck Tomorrow is a pulse-pounding crime drama and the debut feature film of Taiwanese-American director Justin Lin, most notably of the Fast & Furious franchise. The film centers on a group of over-achieving Asian-American high school seniors who enjoy a newfound sense of power and brotherhood when they embrace criminal activities as their main extra-curriculars.


Accomplished high school student Ben (Parry Shen) seems to excel at almost everything except winning over his dream girl Stephanie (Karin Anna Cheung). When he begins an unlikely friendship with trouble-seeking tough guy Daric (Roger Fan), Ben and his friend Virgil (Jason Tobin) become involved in petty crime that gets increasingly dangerous, with his various illegal ventures extending to include Stephanie and her wealthy college beau Steve (John Cho). As the stakes get higher and the wild parties and drugs take their toll, Ben grows more desperate to get out and leave behind a life of crime for good. But before he can, a final devastating turn leads to a shocking finale that will stay with you long after you leave the theatre.


Among the first mainstream Hollywood films by an Asian-American director, the film was initially criticized for its violent representation of Asian-American teens, but has come to be celebrated for the intensity of its story and complexity of its characters, who have the right to be flawed, multidimensional human beings. Defying all stereotypes, Better Luck Tomorrow ultimately offers a disturbing look at the dark side of four wealthy, disaffected Southern California suburbanites.


Director Justin Lin also considers the film to be a prequel to the Fast & Furious franchise because Virgil's carefree older cousin Han is also the character Han Seoul-Oh, who is introduced in the 2006 film The Fast and the Furious: Tokyo Drift.

films.sort_key: Poetics of Life and Death: Short Films from Syria, Lebanon, and Palestine
films.description:
Presented in collaboration with the Southwest Asia and North Africa Program (SWANA), this program features a selection of short films  from Syria, Lebanon, and Palestine that screened at the Festival de Cine Libanés 2026 in Mexico City. 


There will be a Q&A with festival director Ginger Jabbour and select filmmakers to follow the screening.


The program will feature:


The Prison (Syria)

Directed by Shaam Joli, 14 minutes

Based on a true story, The Prison follows a young Syrian student who is arrested on the street and imprisoned without warning. Subjected to torture and sexual violence, she struggles to survive a system designed to silence and dehumanize her. The film gives a face and a voice to the countless victims, too often reduced to mere statistics.

 

There Are Rumors That We Left (Syria-Lebanon)

Directed by Joyce Oska, 13 minutes

Amid the war, Joelle, a young single mother, struggles to protect her daughter after a terrorist attack destroys a nearby school bus. When a travel ban leaves her eight-year-old daughter stranded, Joelle has no choice but to smuggle her across the Syrian-Lebanese border.

 

A Dream Pointing to Aadchit (Lebanon)

Directed by Ghinwa Yassine, 18 minutes

Haunted by a recurring dream in which her grandfather tends the land of her childhood, G decides to return to Aadchit, a small village in southern Lebanon, where she discovers that the war has forever transformed her memories.

 

Abu Jabal (Palestine)

Directed by Bisan Owda, 19 minutes

After seven months of displacement, Tahani and her daughter Sidra return to the ruins of their home in Khan Yunis. Confronted with devastating loss, they find their only refuge beside the grave of Abu Jabal—Tahani’s son and Sidra’s brother, whose name means “mountain” in Arabic.

 

Adas Falesteen (Palestine)

Directed by Samar Taher Lulu & Hamid Khalil Elhusseini, 7 minutes

Amid the famine caused by the war on Gaza, a Palestinian chef transforms his passion for cooking into an act of resistance. Through a community kitchen, he prepares lentil meals for those facing hunger, nourishing not only their bodies but also a shared spirit of solidarity, resilience, and hope.

films.name: Our Land (Nuestra Tierra)
films.description:
In October 2009, Javier Chocobar, a member of the indigenous Chuchagasta community in northwest Argentina’s Tucumán Province, tried to defend himself and his people from being forcibly evicted from their land by a local landowner and two former police officers. As a result, the 68-year-old Chocobar was shot and killed, and two other community members were wounded.


In her expansive and enlightening first feature documentary, Argentinean filmmaker Lucrecia Martel (Zama, The Headless Woman) takes a sweeping approach to this tragic true story, triangulating the murder trial of the three men, the lives of Chocobar and his fellow Chuchagasta people, and the centuries-old, colonialist legacy of land and property theft across Latin America. With a ravishing, at times vertiginous visual approach to filming the natural beauty of the contested land, Martel pays cinematic tribute to people whom others systematically tried to erase from history.

films.name: Barbara Forever
films.short_description: An archive-driven exploration of the life, work, and legacy of iconic, pioneering lesbian filmmaker Barbara Hammer.
films.description:
"If we're experimenting with our lives and the way we're going to live, our film and our art should also be experimental. It breaks tradition, and makes you think in a broader way. It's the way I experience the world." – Barbara Hammer


BARBARA FOREVER explores the films, archive, and ongoing cultural impact of experimental filmmaker Barbara Hammer, revealing her ingenious lifelong artistic effort to create and record lesbian histories, personal and societal. Through her own images and words, the film centers Hammer as a prism of the cultural ecosystems around her – through the feminist and queer movements in 1970s San Francisco, the male-dominated New York art world of the 1980s, the New Queer Cinema movement of the 1990s, and expanded LGBTQIA+ representation in art and culture in the 2000s.


Driven by her canon of over eighty films, a vast collection of unreleased archival materials – hundreds of hours of footage, personal photographs and ephemera, and extensive audio interviews – BARBARA FOREVER tells Barbara Hammer’s story through her own voice and visual perspective, making her the expert on her life, vision, and motivations.


Barbara Hammer’s films break taboos around female sexuality, aging, illness, and queer love, often using her own body as a site of exploration and political power. Through the course of the film, she shows us that the personal is not only political, the personal is historical. Looking to Barbara Hammer as one of the first filmmakers to put a full lesbian life on screen that wasn’t there before, her work becomes a blueprint for a new generation of queer and radical artists to write their own histories into existence. This exploration of both Barbara Hammer’s life, work, archive, and her ongoing legacy provides an urgent, necessary story of queer life, feminist history, and American cinema

films.name: Black Zombie
films.short_description: From the flickering screens of Hollywood horror, to the haunted cane fields of colonial Haiti, Black Zombie unearths the buried origins of the zombie, reclaiming it as a symbol of survival and spiritual resistance.
films.description:
Black Zombie digs beneath the blood-soaked spectacle of modern horror to uncover the zombie’s buried and unsettling origins. Long before it became associated with flesh-eating ghouls, the zombie was a living metaphor for slavery: not a monster, but the ultimate victim of colonial power. A symbol of stolen agency was recast as an object of fear, while Black spiritual traditions were distorted, sensationalized, and erased.


Director Maya Annik Bedward traces the evolution of the zombie from colonial Haiti to contemporary Hollywood, reconsidering iconic films like White Zombie, Night of the Living Dead, and The Serpent and the Rainbow alongside archival footage, vérité scenes, and interviews with cultural historians, artists, and genre legends including Yves-Grégory Francois, Mambo Labelle Déesse, Slash, Tom Savini, and Zandashé Brown. Part cultural reckoning, part horror remix, Black Zombie exposes how a figure born from enslavement, spiritual belief, and resistance was transformed into one of pop culture’s most profitable monsters.


In English, French, and Haitian Creole with English subtitles. Part of our "Doc Spots" series. Distributor: Kino Lorber

films.description:
Mel Brooks gives the horror classic a riotous twist in this unforgettable parody of Mary Shelley's 1818 novel and its many film adaptations.

films.name: Malombra
films.description:
Based on the 1881 novel by Antonio Fogazzaro, Malombra (1917) stars the silent film diva Lyda Borelli as an orphaned young woman who comes to live in a castle with her uncle prior to her wedding day. She begins to read letters written by her late aunt Cecilia and discovers that Cecilia was driven to her death by her uncle.


Marina develops a profound connection with the spirit of Cecilia, which begins to possess Marina and drive her to exact revenge. Narrative quickly becomes secondary to Borelli's enchanting and dramatically physical performance of a woman possessed.


Long thought to be lost, Malombra was restored in 1996 by Cineteca di Bologna from the first reel of a positive nitrate print with Italian intertitles from Fondo Pegoretti and a vintage positive nitrate print with Spanish intertitles from Fondo Pereda preserved by Archivio Nacional de la Imagen – Sodre. You can explore the restored print more closely in Barbara Flueckiger's Timeline of Historical Film Colors.


Malombra will be presented at Cornell Cinema with a live score by acclaimed musicians Donald Sosin and Joanna Seaton.

For twenty years, Donald Sosin and Joanna Seaton have been among the only major performers in the US creating vocals as well as instrumentals for classic silent films and have won high praise from experts in the field, as well as enthusiastic supporters of all ages everywhere they appear. Donald and Joanna (who obtained a Theatre Arts degree from Cornell) bring their unique blend of keyboards, vocals, and percussion to major film festivals—New York, San Francisco, Seattle, Telluride, TriBeCa and more—and to MoMA, BAM, AFI Silver, the Thailand Silent Film Festival, and others. films.description:
In Everyone Is Lying to You for Money, actor and author Ben McKenzie turns investigator, pulling back the curtain on the cryptocurrency industry and the culture of hype, misinformation, and speculation that fueled its explosive rise. What began as a promise of financial freedom has evolved into a volatile ecosystem rife with fraud and reckless gambling, carrying with it devastating consequences for everyday people.


Through firsthand reporting, expert interviews, and a clear-eyed examination of major collapses and scandals, the film traces how crypto became one of the most aggressively marketed financial products of the modern era—and how warning signs were ignored, dismissed, or deliberately obscured. As fortunes are made and lost, Everyone Is Lying to You for Money asks a sobering question: who benefits from the chaos, and who is left to clean up the damage?


Accessible, urgent, and often darkly ironic, the film is both a cautionary tale and a call for accountability—cutting through the noise to expose a system built on speculation, influence, and belief rather than truth.


After the screening, there will be a panel discussion with Gili Vidan, Assistant Professor of Information Science, and Owen Marshall, Visiting Assistant Professor in the Departments of Science & Technology Studies and Information Science at Cornell.

films.short_description: God and Satan wager on the soul of a learned and prayerful alchemist as part of their eternal war over Earth.
films.description:
Cornell Cinema is thrilled to welcome the Invincible Czars back to Sage Chapel to celebrate 100 years of the silent masterpiece FAUST (1926)!


The Invincible Czars will perform a brand new electrifying score that brings this classic film to life for contemporary audiences by marrying new and old elements of classical music, bossa nova, and even a touch of heavy metal and incorporating a mix of instruments like flute, violin and electric guitar. Their annual performance at Sage Chapel is a highlight of the spooky season in Ithaca!


Faust—directed by the legendary F.W. Murnau—centers on an elderly alchemist named Faust (Gösta Ekman) who makes a pact with the demon Mephisto (Emil Jannings) to gain the power to protect his village from plague. Faust soon succumbs to temptation and asks Mephisto to restore his youth and help him acquire all the hedonistic pleasures that earth can offer. Eventually, his love affair with a young woman named Gretchen (Camilla Horn) leads to tragic and devastating consequences for them both.


Faust is the quintessential “deal with the devil” tale based on a centuries-old European legend and Johann Wofgang Goethe’s 1808 play, which is considered one of Germany’s greatest literary works. The play also inspired the famous opera by Charles Guonod which director F.W. Murnau used as a map for his 1926 film. (Fun fact: Faust is the opera being presented in Gaston Leroux’s Phantom of the Opera, which Cornell Cinema featured at Sage Chapel last year.) Virtually every "sell your soul" type story from the film Crossroads to songs like "The Devil Went Down To Georgia" owes a debt to Faust — whether their creators realize it or not!


The event will take place at Sage Chapel, Ho Plaza, Ithaca, New York. More information about parking and directions is available on our website.


Special event pricing applies and all tickets must be purchased online in advance.We expect a sell-out crowd, so please get your tickets early to avoid disappointment!


The Invincible Czars have made a name for themselves among horror and classic film lovers in the US and Canada with their original, tastefully modern live soundtracks for silent films which they started creating for the original Alamo Drafthouse in their hometown of Austin, TX in 2007, though they began making their whacky brand of cinematic rock in 2003. They are great at using music and sound to transform century-old movies into immersive and engaging experiences that allow audiences to approach, appreciate, and enjoy the depth and innovation of classic silent film. Czars shows are a lot of fun with opportunities for audience participation and costumery.

films.description:
Most people dream of a better future. Pedro, an aspiring social worker, is no different. But as a blind, undocumented immigrant, Pedro faces political restrictions to obtain his college degree, secure a job in his field, and support his family. As he finally graduates, uncertainty looms over Pedro. What starts as a journey to provide mental health care for his community ultimately transforms into Pedro’s path towards his own healing.


Directed by queer, undocumented filmmaker, writer, and community organizer Set Hernandez, Unseen is a visually innovative, audio-centric documentary that reimagines the accessibility of cinema, while exploring the intersections of immigration, disability, and mental health. films.name: A Page of Madness
films.short_description: A man takes a job at an asylum with hopes of freeing his imprisoned wife.
films.description:
Japanese director Teinosuke Kinugasa’s A Page of Madness (Japanese title: Kurutta Ichipeiji) is among the most unsettling, visually striking, and criminally underseen films of the silent era.


Set inside an insane asylum, the film centers on a man (Masao Inoue) who takes a job as a janitor with hopes of freeing his wife (Yoshie Nakagawa), who is imprisoned as a patient there. A series of fragmented, hallucinatory flashbacks relate the events that caused the woman's descent into madness—including the loss of a baby—and her husband's subsequent feelings of guilt and responsibility. As the man attempts to reconnect with his mentally unstable wife through the bars of the asylum, his own sanity begins to waver and an unexpected encounter with his daughter may be the thing that pushes him over the edge.


Throughout the film, the impending sense of a descent into madness is amplified by inventive cinematography by Kōhei Sugiyama, who uses double, triple, and even quadruple exposures to disorient, disturb, and delve the viewer into memories, madness, and subjective subconsciousness. According to Michael Atkinson in an essay for the 2017 San Francisco Silent Film Festival, A Page of Madness "may be the best—that is, the most fascinating and the most terrifying—madhouse movie ever made and makes all other efforts at visualizing the subjective experience of mental and emotional disarray look childish and campy by comparison."

films.name: Black Zombie
films.short_description: From the flickering screens of Hollywood horror, to the haunted cane fields of colonial Haiti, Black Zombie unearths the buried origins of the zombie, reclaiming it as a symbol of survival and spiritual resistance.
films.description:
Black Zombie digs beneath the blood-soaked spectacle of modern horror to uncover the zombie’s buried and unsettling origins. Long before it became associated with flesh-eating ghouls, the zombie was a living metaphor for slavery: not a monster, but the ultimate victim of colonial power. A symbol of stolen agency was recast as an object of fear, while Black spiritual traditions were distorted, sensationalized, and erased.


Director Maya Annik Bedward traces the evolution of the zombie from colonial Haiti to contemporary Hollywood, reconsidering iconic films like White Zombie, Night of the Living Dead, and The Serpent and the Rainbow alongside archival footage, vérité scenes, and interviews with cultural historians, artists, and genre legends including Yves-Grégory Francois, Mambo Labelle Déesse, Slash, Tom Savini, and Zandashé Brown. Part cultural reckoning, part horror remix, Black Zombie exposes how a figure born from enslavement, spiritual belief, and resistance was transformed into one of pop culture’s most profitable monsters.


In English, French, and Haitian Creole with English subtitles. Part of our "Doc Spots" series. Distributor: Kino Lorber

Their sinister plot comes to fruition when the unsuspecting Carrie is named prom queen—but little do they know that Carrie has been working hard to harness her telekinetic powers and unleashes her own revenge on all those who have bullied her in one of the most memorable sequences in cinema history.

films.name: Arts Unplugged: Deaf President Now!
films.short_description: Discover the story of the greatest civil rights movement most people have never heard about. During eight tumultuous days in 1988 at the world's only Deaf university, four students must find a way to lead a revolution—and change the course of history.
films.description:
The College of Arts & Sciences will present two free films at Cornell Cinema on Thursday, November 5, as part of a three-day event: "Language, memory, future: Celebrating 250 years of language in our region.” 


Screenings will take place at 4:30pm and 7:30pm. The program will feature:


- Deaf President Now! (2025, dir. Nyle DiMarco & Davis Guggenheim) at 4:30 p.m., followed by,

- Fancy Dance (2023, dir. Erica Tremblay), which centers on a woman on the Seneca-Cayuga reservation searching for her missing sister, whom her niece is desperate to find before her first powwow, at 7:30 p.m.


Deaf President Now! recounts the eight days of historic protests held at Gallaudet University in 1988 after the school’s board of trustees appointed a hearing president over several very qualified Deaf candidates. After a week of rallies, boycotts and protests, the students of Gallaudet University triumph as the hearing president resigns and beloved dean Dr. I. King Jordan becomes the university’s first Deaf president. The protests marked a pivotal moment in civil rights history, with an impact that extended well beyond the Gallaudet campus, and paved the way for the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). 


Deaf President Now! features exclusive interviews with the five key figures of the movement, including the Gallaudet Four — Jerry Covell, Bridgetta Bourne-Firl, Tim Rarus and Greg Hlibok — alongside I. King Jordan, as well as archival and scripted elements. The film also incorporates an experimental narrative approach called Deaf Point of View, using impressionistic visual photography and intricate sound design to thrust the audience into the Deaf experience.


The screening will also feature a special Zoom Q&A with Greg Hlibok, one of the student leaders featured in the film.


Free and open to all! Sponsored by College of Arts & Sciences’ Arts Unplugged series. The Arts Unplugged event will also include a Nov. 6 keynote address by Daniel Kaufman, director of the Endangered Language Alliance and associate professor at Queens College, and an evening of performances, as well as an academic conference Nov. 7.


The College of Arts & Sciences’ Arts Unplugged series brings research and creative works into the public sphere for discussion and inspiration. These engaging events invite a broad audience to explore the work of scholars, faculty and creative luminaries across disciplines in arts and sciences to celebrate the impact that work continues to have on humanity.

films.description:
Beyond its obvious cultural significance as the only classic film noir directed by a woman—the incomparable actress Ida Lupino—The Hitch-Hiker is perhaps better remembered as simply one of the most nightmarish motion pictures of the 1950s.


Inspired by the true-life murder spree of Billy Cook, The Hitch-Hiker is the tension-laden saga of two men on a camping trip (Edmond O'Brien and Frank Lovejoy) who are held captive by a homicidal drifter (William Talman). He forces them, at gunpoint, to embark on a grim joyride across the Mexican desert.


Renegade filmmaking at its finest, The Hitch-Hiker was independently produced, which allowed Lupino and ex-husband/producer Collier Young to work from a treatment by blacklisted writer Daniel Mainwaring, and tackle an incident that was too brutal for the major studios to even consider.

Sarah (Robin Tunney) has always been different. When she transfers to St. Benedict's Academy, a Catholic school in Los Angeles, she immediately falls in with a crew of outsiders: a group of three wannabe witches, who happen to be seeking a fourth member for their rituals.


Like Sarah, Bonnie (Neve Campbell), Rochelle (Rachel True) and Nancy (Fairuza Balk) all have troubled backgrounds, which combined with their nascent powers lead to dangerous consequences. When a minor spell causes a fellow student to lose her hair, the girls are consumed — ready to wield their powers against all who dare to cross them, be they teachers, rivals or meddlesome parents.


Embraced as a cult and queer classic, The Craft is a spooky and fun fantasy-horror about being an outsider and remains an absolute must-watch for fans of the genre.

films.name: One in a Million
films.short_description: Filmed over 10 years, one girl's epic journey from Syria to Germany and back again. She and her family navigate war, exile, and heartbreak in a foreign land, illuminating the complexities of the refugee experience.
films.description:
Filmed over ten years, One in a Million follows Israa from childhood to adulthood on an extraordinary journey from war-torn Syria to Germany — and back again. We first meet her at age 11 as she and her family prepare to cross the Aegean Sea, risking everything in search of safety and a better life in Europe. What unfolds is a deeply personal chronicle of war, exile, and heartbreak, as Israa grows up navigating adolescence, identity, and belonging far from the home she was forced to leave. As she settles into life in Germany, new freedoms collide with the stabilizing pull of Syrian traditions, testing family bonds and reshaping her sense of self.


Co-directed by Itab Azzam and Jack MacInnes, the film bears witness to the remarkable trust between filmmakers and family, following Israa and her loved ones across borders, cultures, and shifting circumstances. An intimate and nuanced coming-of-age story, One in a Million illuminates the complexities of the refugee experience while asking a universal question: what does it truly mean to call a place home?


Free admission! Sponsored by the Migrations Program and the Southwest Asia and North Africa Program at the Mario Einaudi Center for International Studies.

films.name: The Hitch-Hiker
films.short_description: Roy and Gilbert's fishing trip takes a terrifying turn when the hitchhiker they pick up turns out to be a sociopath on the run from the law. He's killed before, and he lets the two know that as soon as they're no longer useful, he'll kill again. The two friends plot an escape, but the hitchhiker's peculiar physical affliction, an eye that never closes even when he sleeps, makes it impossible for them to tell when they can make a break for it.
films.description:
Beyond its obvious cultural significance as the only classic film noir directed by a woman—the incomparable actress Ida Lupino—The Hitch-Hiker is perhaps better remembered as simply one of the most nightmarish motion pictures of the 1950s.


Inspired by the true-life murder spree of Billy Cook, The Hitch-Hiker is the tension-laden saga of two men on a camping trip (Edmond O'Brien and Frank Lovejoy) who are held captive by a homicidal drifter (William Talman). He forces them, at gunpoint, to embark on a grim joyride across the Mexican desert.


Renegade filmmaking at its finest, The Hitch-Hiker was independently produced, which allowed Lupino and ex-husband/producer Collier Young to work from a treatment by blacklisted writer Daniel Mainwaring, and tackle an incident that was too brutal for the major studios to even consider.


In English and Spanish with English subtitles. Part of our "Noirvember" series. Courtesy: Kino Lorber

films.name: The Wicker Man
films.short_description: Police sergeant Neil Howie is called to an island village in search of a missing girl whom the locals claim never existed. The investigation is further complicated as Howie’s religious views clash with those of the island’s residents.
films.description:
After receiving an anonymous letter about a missing 12-year-old girl, devoutly Christian Police Sergeant Neil Howie (Edward Woodward) travels by seaplane to a remote Scottish island to investigate. But the islanders welcome neither his badge nor religious devotion, for Lord Summerisle (Christopher Lee) and his devoted followers worship only the pagan gods of old. Howie fears for the missing girl's life and follows every possible lead to find her. As the investigation progresses, however, and the townspeople begin to deny the girl’s existence, Sergeant Howie wonders if the disappearance isn’t the only thing the townspeople are covering up…. 


One of the most iconic British horror films, Robin Hardy tackles paganism with style in the first installment of what will become The Wicker Man trilogy. This cult classic—famously remade by Nicholas Cage in 2006—has now restored in 4K by Studiocanal at Silver Salt Restoration UK from the original 35mm negative.


Part of our "The Uncanny" film series. Distributor: Rialto Pictures

films.short_description: Dr. Henry Jekyll experiments with scientific means of revealing the hidden, dark side of man and releases a murderer from within himself.
films.description:
Cornell Cinema is pleased to partner with the Cornell Chamber Orchestra to present a live-to-picture performance of the 1920 silent film Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde in Bailey Hall, featuring an original score by a team of film composers led by Sheldon Mirowitz and conductor Gabriela Gómez Estévez, performed in synchronization with the film.

 

Based on the 1886 novel by Robert Louis Stevenson, Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde centers on a career-focused doctor’s ill-fated experimentations with the dual personalities—good and evil—that he believes define all human beings. Prompted by criticism from his girlfriend’s father, the gentlemanly Dr. Jekyll begins to explore his darker side and develops a potion that transforms him into a grotesque alter ego named Hyde. Driven by the thrill of Hyde’s dark indulgences, Dr. Jekyll begins to lead a double life as a kindly doctor by day and an increasingly depraved creature by night… with ultimately fatal consequences.


The event will take place at Bailey Hall, 230 Garden Ave, Ithaca, NY 14850.

 

Free admission! All are welcome and no tickets or pre-registration are required.


﻿Presented by the Department of Music in collaboration with Cornell Cinema and Wharton Studio Museum.

 

Part of our "Altered States in Silent Cinema" series, which is presented in collaboration with the Wharton Studio Museum and Cinemapolis as part of Silent Movie Month in Ithaca.

films.name: The Killing
films.description:
Stanley Kubrick’s account of an ambitious racetrack robbery is one of Hollywood’s tautest, twistiest noirs. Career criminal Johnny Clay (Sterling Hayden) recruits a sharpshooter, a crooked police officer, a bartender and a betting teller named George, among others, for one last job before he goes straight and gets married. But when George tells his restless wife about the scheme to steal millions from the racetrack where he works, she hatches a plot of her own.


Written by pulp novelist Jim Thompson and featuring suspenseful tracking shots and a phenomenal cast, including Sterling Hayden, Coleen Gray, Timothy Carey, Elisha Cook Jr., and Marie Windsor, The Killing is Kubrick at his finest: a jaunty thriller and a cold-blooded punch to the gut—that also reportedly provided key inspiration for Quentin Tarantino's debut feature Reservoir Dogs (1992).

films.name: The Color of Pomegranates
films.short_description: The life of the revered 18th-century Armenian poet and musician Sayat-Nova. Portraying events in the life of the artist from childhood up to his death, the movie addresses in particular his relationships with women, including his muse. The production tells Sayat-Nova's dramatic story by using both his poems and largely still camerawork, creating a work hailed as revolutionary by Mikhail Vartanov.
films.description:
A breathtaking fusion of poetry, ethnography, and cinema, Sergei Parajanov’s masterwork overflows with unforgettable images and sounds. In a series of tableaux that blend the tactile with the abstract, The Color of Pomegranates revives the splendors of Armenian culture through the story of the eighteenth-century troubadour Sayat-Nova, charting his intellectual, artistic, and spiritual growth through iconographic compositions rather than traditional narrative.


The film’s tapestry of folklore and metaphor departed from the realism that dominated the Soviet cinema of its era, leading authorities to block its distribution, with rare underground screenings presenting it in a restructured form. This restored edition features the cut closest to Parajanov’s original vision, bringing new life to one of cinema’s most enigmatic meditations on art and beauty.


The Color of Pomegranates was restored by The Film Foundation’s World Cinema Project and the Cineteca di Bologna, in association with the National Cinema Centre of Armenia and Gosfilmofond of Russia, and funded by the Material World Charitable Foundation.


Free admission! Sponsored by the Department of Near Eastern Studies.


In Armenian, Azerbaijani, and Georgian with English subtitles. Part of our "Near Eastern Studies" series. Distributor: Janus Films

films.name: Sound of Falling
films.description:
Mascha Schilinski’s transcendent Sound of Falling tracks the lives of four adolescent girls Alma, Erika, Angelika, Lenka who each spend their youth in the same farmhouse over the course of the last century. Fragments from a hundred years in one farmhouse coalesce into a cinematic flood of memory—their desires and distress, their secrets and truths, their encounters with another’s gaze and defiant gaze in return.


Though separated by time, far-reaching resonances emerge as echoes of experience linger in this sensual and sensory film, which won the Grand Jury Prize at the 2025 Cannes Film Festival. Sound of Falling invites audiences to witness an eternal summer, a constant now, and to ask: what is looking back at us from the past—or perhaps even from the future?

films.name: National Treasure
films.description:
What better way to celebrate America's 250th birthday than by stealing the Declaration of Independence?


Amateur historian and cryptographer Benjamin Franklin Gates (Nicholas Cage) has devoted much of his life to searching for a mysterious treasure trove hidden by the America's Founding Fathers during the Revolutionary War. Together with modern treasure hunter Ian Howe (Sean Bean), he discovers a long-lost Colonial shipwreck in the Arctic Circle that contains a clue linking the treasure to the Declaration of Independence. But the sinister Ian wants the treasure for himself and is ready to destroy anyone that gets in his way.


Determined to find and protect the treasure before Ian and his henchmen, Gates must steal one of America's most sacred and guarded documents or let it—and a key clue to the mystery—fall into dangerous hands. Together with his computer geek sidekick Riley (Justin Bartha), the reluctant archivist Abigail Chase (Diane Kruger), and his estranged father Patrick (Jon Voigt), Gates embarks on a thrilling race against time to decipher one of the greatest mysteries in human history.


And we can all agree that the inimitable Nicholas Cage remains one of America's greatest national treasures!

films.description:
Our once-a-semester Mystery Screening is a risk—and a study break—worth taking.


Cornell Cinema will celebrate the end of the semester with a special surprise film screening. Don't miss your chance to discover a new favorite or be delighted by a classic film with our Cornell Cinema community. The secret will only be revealed when the screening begins!


Previous films have included Jonathan Lynn's My Cousin Vinny (1992), Fritz Lang's M (1931),Jono McLeod's My Old School (2022), Brian de Palma's Blow Out (1981), Sydney Pollack's The Way We Were (1973), and Milos Forman's The Fireman's Ball (1967). 


Tickets are $5 each or free for All-Access Passholders.


What will our next mystery movie be? Stay tuned for more details as we get closer to the screening!
